svg.title: Hipparchus, lunar parallax from two reports
svg.desc: Hellespont and Alexandria see the Moon along different lines. The Sun is so far that its direction is drawn as one shared direction. The angle between the Moon sightlines is enlarged on purpose. Hipparchus used reports. He was not standing at both places.
svg.text: Same Sun, two places, a nearer Moon
Angles much too large. Solar parallax drawn as nothing.
Baseline: the latitudes between the reports, not a voyage Hipparchus made twice.
Total at the Hellespont. At Alexandria, about four-fifths of the Sun's diameter still showed.
That is a fraction of the diameter, not four-fifths of the area. The eclipse date is uncertain.
